Under MIDH, 50% subsidy: anti-bird or anti-hail nets Rs.50 per sq.m (subsidy Rs.25), up to 10,000 sq.m; their permanent support structure Rs.20 per sq.m (Rs.10), up to 2 ha; fencing Rs.300 per running metre (Rs.150), up to 1,000 m, only with another MIDH component; fruit or bunch covers Rs.50,000 per ha (Rs.25,000), up to 2 ha; vegetable support system Rs.20,000 per ha (Rs.10,000), up to 2 ha.

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH individual farm pond subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. Individual farm pond for horticulture under MIDH: standard size 20m x 20m x 3m (1,200 cu.m), unit cost Rs.1.50 lakh; subsidy 50%, which is Rs.75,000, worked at Rs.62.50 per cu.m of actual volume, including 300 micron plastic or RCC lining. Unlined ponds (black cotton soil only) cost 30% less. Smaller ponds pro rata. Released after completion with fencing and sign board, on joint inspection; complete within 60 days of sanction. Existing RCC-lined and old incomplete ponds are not eligible.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH community water harvesting tank subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH new orchard area expansion subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. New orchards (area expansion) under MIDH: up to 40% of the total cost of plant material, inputs, supports and INM/IPM, paid over two years in a 60:40 ratio. The second year is paid only if at least 80% of plants survive. Paid by DBT. Land must be certified from the pattadar passbook or adangal. Per-hectare unit costs differ by crop and spacing.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

text: Andhra Pradesh. Mushroom under MIDH: small mushroom production unit of 200 sq.ft, cost norm Rs.2 lakh, 50% assistance, up to 5 units per beneficiary, bank loan not needed. Larger production, spawn or compost units (Rs.20 to 30 lakh): 40% credit-linked back-ended subsidy for the private sector.

source.doc: Andhra Pradesh Horticulture Department, MIDH implementation guidelines 2025

subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH farm gate pack house and cold room subsidy
text: Andhra Pradesh. Farm gate pack house (9m x 6m) under MIDH: unit cost limited to Rs.4.80 lakh, 50% assistance. Add-on farm gate cold room up to 10 MT: 35% of unit cost, unit cost limited to Rs.20 lakh (solar with battery), Rs.8 lakh (thermal storage on grid), Rs.12 lakh (biomass) or Rs.5 lakh (conventional grid). Land must be owned or on a registered lease of at least 10 years.

subject: Andhra Pradesh paddy procurement rules KMS 2026-27
text: Andhra Pradesh. Paddy procurement, Kharif Marketing Season 2026-27 (Kharif and Rabi): MSP for FAQ paddy Rs.2,441 per quintal common, Rs.2,461 Grade A. Procured only from farmers (tenants included) registered in e-Panta through the Rythu Seva Kendram, at procurement centres in the RSKs; payment Aadhaar-based from e-Panta data. FAQ paddy moisture up to 17%; paddy not meeting FAQ is to be dried and cleaned, not refused outright. The farmer may choose the rice mill, but transport is paid at the lowest slab in the area and beyond 40 km is not paid. Millers buying privately must pay at least MSP into the farmer's bank account.

subject: Tamil Nadu CM Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam farmer welfare benefits
text: Tamil Nadu. Chief Minister's Uzhavar Pathukappu Thittam: for agricultural labourers (including fisheries, dairy, horticulture, sericulture, cattle, poultry, plantation work) and small or marginal farmers owning up to 2.5 acres wet or 5 acres dry land who farm directly, cultivating tenants included, aged 18 to 65. Benefits for the member: marriage assistance Rs.8,000 (male) or Rs.10,000 (female); old age pension Rs.1,200 a month; Rs.1,000 a month while incapacitated by TB, cancer, HIV, dialysis, fractures and other listed illnesses; accident death Rs.1 lakh (landless labourers Rs.2 lakh), injury Rs.20,000 to Rs.1 lakh; natural death Rs.20,000 (landless Rs.30,000); funeral Rs.2,500 (landless Rs.10,000); paralysis Rs.50,000. Dependants: education help Rs.1,250 to Rs.6,750 a year, marriage assistance as above.

subject: Tamil Nadu Agricultural Engineering Department machinery hire charges
text: Tamil Nadu. Agricultural Engineering Department machinery hired to farmers, 2026-27, per hour including diesel: bulldozer Rs.1,230; tractor Rs.500; mini tractor Rs.460; paddy combine harvester wheel type Rs.1,160, track type Rs.1,880; backhoe with front-end loader (JCB type) Rs.890; mini backhoe Rs.650; crawler excavator Rs.1,910; sugarcane harvester with infielders Rs.5,120; truck coconut hoist Rs.450; tractor with implements, pumpset or paddy mobile dryer Rs.500 (dryer burner fuel and labour extra); heavy chain saw Rs.85 (fuel and labour extra). Minor irrigation machinery: rotary drill Rs.130 per metre, percussion drill Rs.300 a day, mini drill Rs.70 per metre, hand boring set Rs.30 per metre, rock blasting Rs.250 per blast, resistivity meter Rs.500 per point, electrical logger Rs.1,000 per bore hole; for these the farmer pays diesel, labour, pipes, pebbles and transport. Machinery goes to farmers who pay in advance; book on e-Vaadagai 2.0 in the Uzhavar App, or ask the block Assistant Engineer or Junior Engineer of the Agricultural Engineering Department. For private hirers and contractors, a 2022 order (G.O.(Ms).No.61 of 15.03.2022) set higher rates: excavator Rs.2,400, backhoe Rs.1,250, bulldozer Rs.1,550; any later revision of those is not held.

Wheat free in place of rice, up to 10 kg in Chennai and district headquarters and 5 kg elsewhere. Sugar 500 g per person, up to 2 kg, at Rs.13.50 a kg for AAY and Rs.25 for others; sugar-option cards get 3 kg more in place of rice. Tur dal 1 kg at Rs.30. Palmolein 1 litre at Rs.25. SC and ST farmers with rainfed land and no irrigation: a borewell or tubewell with an electric motor or solar pumpset at 100% subsidy, up to Rs.8 lakh per farmer, for 300 farmers in 2026-27. subject: Andhra Pradesh MIDH horticulture machinery subsidy

Tractor up to 20 PTO HP: 2WD cost Rs.4 lakh, subsidy up to Rs.2 lakh (others Rs.1.60 lakh); 4WD cost Rs.4.90 lakh, up to Rs.2.45 lakh (others Rs.1.96 lakh). Power tiller 8 to 11 BHP: cost Rs.2 lakh, up to Rs.1 lakh (others Rs.80,000); above 11 BHP: cost Rs.2.40 lakh, up to Rs.1.20 lakh (others Rs.1 lakh). Powered knapsack or Taiwan sprayer above 16 litres: cost Rs.20,000, up to Rs.10,000 (others Rs.8,000). Tractor boom sprayer: cost Rs.82,000, up to Rs.41,000 (others Rs.33,000). Tractor air-assisted sprayer: cost Rs.2.76 lakh, up to Rs.1.38 lakh (others Rs.1.10 lakh). Electrostatic sprayer: cost Rs.5 lakh, up to Rs.2.50 lakh (others Rs.2 lakh). subject: Tamil Nadu oil palm subsidy NMEO-OP 2026-27

Oil palm (NMEO-OP), 2026-27: planting material subsidy Rs.20,000 per ha for indigenous and Rs.29,000 per ha for imported seedlings (150 seedlings per ha), supplied through the allotted oil palm firm. During the 4-year gestation period, 50% of maintenance cost up to Rs.5,250 per ha a year and 50% of intercrop inputs up to Rs.5,250 per ha a year, Rs.42,000 per ha in all. Tools at 50% up to: oil palm cutter Rs.2,500, protective wire mesh Rs.20,000, motorised chisel Rs.15,000, aluminium ladder Rs.5,000, chaff cutter Rs.50,000, tractor trolley Rs.2 lakh. Production incentive Rs.1,000 per tonne of fresh fruit bunches above 8 tonnes per ha from plantations 5 years or older. Register on TNHORTNET.

text: Andhra Pradesh. Subsidy seeds under the various schemes are given at the Rythu Seva Kendram through the D-Krishi app: the RSK in-charge identifies the farmer, who is authenticated by biometrics, face recognition or an OTP to the Aadhaar-linked mobile, both when paying the non-subsidy share and when taking the seed; a message with the registration ID goes to that mobile. Allocation runs state to district to mandal to RSK, and AP Seeds supplies RSKs directly. The subsidy rate for each crop is not in this order.

subject: Andhra Pradesh fishing ban relief eligibility
text: Andhra Pradesh, Marine Fishing Ban Relief, who can get it (G.O.Rt.No.139 of 22.04.2025). Crew of mechanized, motorized and traditional crafts registered under the M.S. Act 1958 on or before 14 April of the year, with a valid APMFR Act 1995 licence for the current Fasli year. Boats under the HSD oil subsidy must have drawn at least 1,000 litres (mechanized) or 100 litres (motorized) in the previous year; all sea-going boats qualify whatever their HSD drawal. Not eligible: those covered by another government DBT scheme or by the NTR Bharosa fishermen pension; family income above Rs.1.20 lakh (rural) or Rs.1.44 lakh (urban) a year; land above 3 acres wet or 10 acres dry or 10 acres together; a family four-wheeler (taxi, tractor, auto exempt); electricity use above 300 units a month; in municipal areas, a house site of 1,000 sq.ft or more; a family member in government service, drawing a government pension, or paying income tax. Six-step validation applies.

subject: Tamil Nadu price support scheme pulses and copra quality norms

subject: Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivator Rights Card (CCRC) for tenant farmers
text: Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivator Rights Act, 2019 (Act 30 of 2019). A tenant (cultivator) and land owner sign an agreement in the form of a Crop Cultivator Rights Card for 11 months, countersigned by the Village Revenue Officer at the Village Secretariat, who must issue it within 3 days, with a copy to the owner. With the card the cultivator gets undisturbed possession for the period even if the land is sold, crop loans from banks and cooperatives (the bank may not ask for other documents and may not attach the land for the cultivator's dues), crop insurance, crop damage relief and other government benefits; SC, ST, BC and minority cultivators also get Rythu Bharosa. The owner keeps ownership, revenue records are not changed, the owner can end the agreement only if the terms are broken, with two months' written notice, and can take loans other than crop loans on the land. The cultivator must vacate at the end, use the land only for farming and repay the crop loan after harvest. Appeals: Tahsildar, then Sub-Collector or RDO, then Joint Collector, each within 7 days. Government land and land assigned to the poor are excluded. Read from a scanned gazette copy. The Act comes into force on a date the government notifies; that notification is not held.

subject: Andhra Pradesh conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural use (NALA repeal)
text: Andhra Pradesh. The Agricultural Land (Conversion for Non-Agricultural Purposes) Act, 2006 (the NALA Act, with its conversion tax) is repealed with effect from 3 September 2025, first by Ordinance No.5 of 2025 and then by L.A. Bill No.29 of 2025, introduced on 26 September 2025. Land use is now regulated by local bodies and urban development authorities under their own laws, such as the AP Metropolitan Region and Urban Development Authorities Act, 2016, which levy development charges. Applications pending under the old Act are decided under it, and conversion tax already assessed can still be recovered. Unauthorised layouts are treated as validly converted on payment of conversion tax on the basic value of their period, with no penalty or interest, for one year from commencement. subject: PMFBY crop insurance: farmer premium, who can enrol, reporting crop loss
text: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (central scheme, Operational Guidelines 2023). Most a farmer pays, as % of sum insured or the actuarial rate if lower: Kharif food grains and oilseeds 2%; Rabi food grains and oilseeds 1.5%; annual commercial and horticultural crops 5% (Kharif and Rabi); perennial horticultural and commercial crops 5% (pilot). The rest of the premium is paid by the centre and the state. All farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in notified areas can enrol, with land records or the tenancy documents the state allows. Only farmers whose data is uploaded on the national portal and whose premium reaches the insurer by the cut-off date are covered. For localised loss or post-harvest loss, tell the insurer within 72 hours through the Crop Insurance App or the Krishi Rakshak helpline 14447, or through the bank, agriculture office or district officials, giving survey number, crop, area affected and application number.

subject: Kisan Credit Card crop loan interest: 7%, or 4% with prompt repayment (Modified Interest Subvention Scheme)
text: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS), continued for 2025-26: short term crop loans and short term loans for allied activities (animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries, bee keeping) through a Kisan Credit Card, up to an overall limit of Rs.3 lakh, at 7% interest to the farmer; lending institutions get 1.50% interest subvention. Farmers who repay on time get a further 3% a year, so they pay 4%; this is lost if the loan is repaid after one year. For farmers only in animal husbandry, dairy, fisheries or bee keeping the benefit is limited to Rs.2 lakh; the crop loan part gets priority within Rs.3 lakh. Covers public sector banks, private banks (rural and semi-urban branches), small finance banks and computerised PACS ceded with scheduled commercial banks. The documents held cover 2025-26; continuation for 2026-27 is not in them.

subject: Kisan Credit Card rules: who can get one, how the limit is set, collateral (RBI KCC Directions, 2026)
text: RBI (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme) Directions, 2026, dated 19 June 2026, for KCC loans sanctioned from 1 January 2027 (earlier loans follow the old guidelines until maturity or renewal). A KCC is a composite facility for six years covering crop cultivation, allied activities (animal husbandry, fisheries and others), post-harvest and household needs, farm asset maintenance, insurance premium, produce marketing loans and investment credit. Eligible for crop working capital: owner cultivators (individual or joint), tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers, and SHGs and JLGs of farmers. The crop drawing limit for each season is the Scale of Finance notified by the State or District Level Technical Committee times the area, plus 10% of that for post-harvest and household needs, plus 20% for repairs, maintenance, soil testing and advisory services, plus insurance premium; if the Scale of Finance is not yet notified, banks add a 10% notional increase over the previous season's. The short term part is a revolving cash credit with no limit on the number of withdrawals and deposits. Banks must waive collateral security and margin for agricultural loans up to Rs.2 lakh per borrower, and may waive collateral up to Rs.3 lakh for KCC loans with a tie-up for recovery. Investment credit is repayable within six years.

source.doc: Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme) Directions, 2026, FIDD.CO.FSD.BC.No.04/05.05.010/2026-27, 19 June 2026

subject: Fertiliser prices: urea Rs.242 per 45 kg bag; how DAP and other P&K fertiliser subsidy works
text: Urea is sold to every farmer at a maximum retail price fixed by law: Rs.242 for a 45 kg bag of neem coated urea, plus neem coating charges and taxes; sulphur coated urea Rs.254 for a 40 kg bag, plus levies and GST. The Government said in March 2026 there is no proposal to raise the urea price; bags were cut from 50 kg to 45 kg (some to 40 kg) to curb overuse. For DAP and other phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers, the Nutrient Based Subsidy policy (since 01.04.2010) pays a fixed subsidy by nutrient content, set each season; the companies fix the MRP at a reasonable level, monitored by the Government. 28 grades of P&K fertiliser, including DAP, are subsidised. Subsidy is paid to the companies only on actual sales at the shop through a PoS machine after the buyer's Aadhaar is verified; any Aadhaar-authenticated buyer can purchase, on a no-denial basis. subject: e-NAM: selling produce on the National Agriculture Market
text: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market), launched April 2016, links mandis into one online trading platform: 1,656 mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories by March 2026, with over 1.80 crore farmers, 2.73 lakh traders and 4,724 FPOs registered. In an e-NAM mandi the produce goes through digital gate entry, a lot with a unique ID, quality assaying and online bidding; each lot can be tracked on mobile, and the sale money is paid straight into the farmer's registered bank account (NEFT, RTGS, internet banking or UPI). The e-NAM app gives free prices for 247 commodities; the platform works in 12 languages including Telugu and Tamil. Produce stored in a WDRA-accredited warehouse can be sold on e-NAM against an electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipt (e-NWR) without moving it. The Government gives up to Rs.75 lakh per mandi for e-NAM infrastructure. Helpline: 1800 270 0224 (toll free); nam@sfac.in.

subject: Land acquisition compensation and resettlement under the 2013 Act
text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (Central Act 30 of 2013). Market value (section 26) is the highest of: the stamp-duty guideline value for the area, the average sale price of similar land nearby (the higher-priced half of sale deeds in the preceding three years), or the consented amount for private or PPP projects. The market value is multiplied by a factor of 1.00 to 2.00 in rural areas, by distance from urban areas as the State notifies, and 1 in urban areas. Value of trees, buildings and other assets is added, then solatium equal to 100% of that compensation (section 30(1)). In addition, 12% a year on the market value is paid from the date of the Social Impact Assessment notification until the award or possession, whichever is earlier (section 30(3)). Resettlement for affected families (Second Schedule): a house if one is lost (rural: Indira Awas Yojana specification; urban: at least 50 sq m, or at least Rs.1,50,000 instead); for irrigation projects, at least one acre in the command area where possible; a choice of a job in the project, a one-time Rs.5 lakh per family, or an annuity of at least Rs.2,000 a month for 20 years; Rs.3,000 a month for one year to displaced families (plus Rs.50,000 for SC/ST families displaced from Scheduled Areas); Rs.50,000 transport; at least Rs.25,000 for a cattle shed or petty shop.

subject: Tamil Nadu land acquisition multiplication factor for rural land
text: Tamil Nadu, land acquisition under the 2013 Act: the factor by which the market value of rural land is multiplied (G.O.(Ms) No.300, Revenue and Disaster Management, dated 20.09.2017) is 1.25 for a project within 30 km of an urban area, 1.5 beyond 30 km and within 50 km, and 2.00 beyond 50 km. With 100% solatium this means 250%, 300% and 400% of the market value respectively. Tamil Nadu's rules are the Tamil Nadu RFCTLARR Rules, 2017. The Collector is the appropriate Government for public-purpose acquisitions of up to forty acres in the district.

subject: PMFME: subsidy to set up or upgrade a small food processing unit
text: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME), centrally sponsored, launched June 2020. Individual units (individuals, proprietorship or partnership firms, FPOs, NGOs, cooperatives, SHGs, private limited companies) setting up or upgrading a micro food processing unit: credit-linked capital subsidy of 35% of the eligible project cost, up to Rs.10 lakh per unit; the eligible cost is plant and machinery and technical civil work (civil work at most 30%), not land or rent. The applicant puts in at least 10% and the rest is a bank loan; no subsidy on working capital. Common infrastructure for FPOs, SHGs and their federations, cooperatives and government agencies: 35% up to Rs.3 crore, with in-principle bank approval needed before applying. Seed capital for SHG members already in food processing: up to Rs.40,000 per member, at most Rs.4 lakh per SHG, given to the SHG federation and lent on to members for small tools and working capital. Up to 50% grant for branding and marketing for groups. Applications are online on the PMFME portal, with District Resource Persons to help file them; priority for the district's One District One Product item. The scheme outlay is Rs.10,000 crore for 2020-21 to 2025-26; the Ministry's page (updated 06.11.2026) still invites applications.

subject: Amaravati capital region land pooling: plots returned, annuity, loan waiver and pension

Landless poor families get a pension of Rs.5,000 a month for 10 years. The surrender form and the Land Pooling Ownership Certificate need no stamp duty or registration charges.

subject: Subsidy for agricultural drones: SMAM for farmers, Namo Drone Didi for women SHGs
text: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM): individual small and marginal farmers and women farmers get a 50% subsidy, up to Rs.5.00 lakh, to buy a drone; Custom Hiring Centres that rent out drones and other machinery to farmers also get assistance. 2,122 drones were approved for individual farmers and CHCs from 2023-24 to 2025-26 (to 30 November 2025). Namo Drone Didi (central sector scheme, outlay Rs.1,261 crore for 2023-24 to 2025-26): selected women SHGs get 80% of the cost of the drone and accessories, up to Rs.8.0 lakh, to provide spraying of fertilisers and pesticides to farmers on rent; the Cluster Level Federation may borrow the balance under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund with 3% interest subvention. The package includes 4 spare battery sets, spares, a fast charger, 15 days of drone pilot training (for the DGCA pilot licence), one-year insurance and 2 years of maintenance. Of the 500 drones given under Namo Drone Didi in 2023-24, 96 went to SHGs in Andhra Pradesh and 17 in Tamil Nadu. Farmers can also ask the local KVK about drone demonstrations.

subject: PM-KISAN: Rs.6,000 a year to landholding farm families, who qualifies and who is excluded
text: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi, central sector scheme): Rs.6,000 a year paid by the Central Government directly into the bank accounts of eligible landholding farmer families by DBT. A farmer's family means husband, wife and minor children who own cultivable land as per the State's land records; only families whose names are in the land records are paid (except North-East States and Jharkhand). Excluded: institutional landholders; families with a member who is or was a constitutional post holder, Union or State minister, MP, MLA or MLC, mayor of a municipal corporation or chairperson of a district panchayat; serving or retired central or state government, PSU or autonomous body employees and regular local body employees (except Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D); pensioners getting Rs.10,000 a month or more (same exception); anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year; practising doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects; and, for new beneficiaries, NRIs. Eligibility is fixed on land held on 01.02.2019: land bought, gifted or received by partition after that date does not make the buyer eligible, but heirs who inherit on the owner's death are eligible. States certify eligibility on the beneficiary's self-declaration, and a wrong declaration means recovery of the money and penal action.

subject: Soil Health Card scheme: free soil testing and fertiliser advice
text: Soil Health Card scheme (central; part of Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana as 'Soil Health & Fertility' since 2022-23): farm soil samples are collected by trained staff, agriculture department staff or agricultural college students, when there is no standing crop, and tested in approved soil testing laboratories; the farmer is not charged, as the Centre pays Rs.190 a sample for collection, testing and card. The card reports 12 parameters: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and sulphur; zinc, iron, copper, manganese and boron; pH, electrical conductivity and organic carbon; with fertiliser recommendations and any soil amendment needed. The explainer states the aim of a card for every farmer once every two years, and also says a card is issued once every 3 years. Results and cards are on the National Soil Health Card portal. 8,272 soil testing labs exist (1,068 static, 163 mobile, 6,376 mini, 665 village-level, February 2025); FPOs and others may apply to set up village-level labs, approved by the District Level Executive Committee.

subject: Andhra Pradesh: freehold rights on assigned land, dotted land and village service inam land
text: Andhra Pradesh. Under the A.P. Assigned Lands (Prohibition of Transfers) Act, 1977 as amended by Act No.35 of 2023, assignees or their legal heirs may sell assigned agricultural land 20 years after assignment (house sites after 10 years); Tahsildars publish yearly lists of eligible lands. Registrations of such lands were kept in abeyance from 10.08.2024 pending verification. G.O.Ms.No.588, Revenue (Lands-I), 15.09.2026, decides by category: land made freehold strictly as per law (7,85,500 acres) can be registered at once, with the land record changed to Patta and marked 'made freehold'; private patta land wrongly treated as assigned, eligible land not yet processed, land under both Act 35 of 2023 and the Dotted Lands Act, 2017, and lands other than water bodies can also be registered; excess extent beyond the original assignment is limited to the LPM extent (resurveyed villages) or the web-land adangal extent; land assigned less than 20 years ago can be registered only after 20 years (assignments of 2006 or earlier are cleared). Registration stays in abeyance for land made freehold in apparent violation of the Act, where the assignee or heirs are not in possession, where no proof of assignment is available (2,87,153 acres, separate orders to follow), and for some lands already registered against the rules; water course and water body porambokes remain prohibited. Ceiling surplus land assigned to the landless poor is treated like assigned land. Dotted land in the Resurvey Settlement Register with the pattadar's name in web-land and no assignment record is treated as the pattadar's private land and removed from the prohibited list.

subject: Farm machinery subsidy and custom hiring centres under SMAM (revised guidelines, December 2025)
text: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM), part of RKVY, revised operational guidelines dated 18.12.2025, implemented by each State. Machines for individual farmers: 50% of the machine cost for small and marginal farmers, SC and ST farmers, women farmers and farmers of the North Eastern and Himalayan States; 40% for all other farmers; machine-wise maximum assistance as in Annexure-I. If applications exceed the target, States approve them by an online lottery, not first come first served. Expensive machines such as tractors above 40 HP, combine harvesters and sugarcane harvesters are to be supported through Custom Hiring Centres and Farm Machinery Banks rather than individual ownership. Small machines costing up to Rs.10,000 may be sold with on-the-spot subsidy at fairs. Custom Hiring Centres (rural entrepreneurs, SHGs, FPOs, PACS and farmer cooperatives): 40% of project cost for projects up to Rs.250 lakh, as credit-linked back-ended subsidy (projects up to Rs.10 lakh may be exempted, with all payments through banks); projects above Rs.50 lakh need a detailed project report; training is compulsory; 10% of CHC funds are earmarked for SHGs under DAY-NRLM. Agriculture graduates setting up Kisan Drone CHCs get 50% of the drone cost or Rs.5 lakh, whichever is less; a drone CHC needs a 10th pass beneficiary and a trained drone pilot. Village Farm Machinery Banks are for villages with low mechanisation, with not more than one tractor per project.

subject: National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF)
text: National Mission on Natural Farming (centrally sponsored, approved 25 November 2024; outlay Rs.2,481 crore till 2025-26, Centre and State sharing 60:40 in most States): natural farming clusters in 15,000 willing gram panchayats, to reach 1 crore farmers and start natural farming on 7.5 lakh ha. 10,000 Bio-input Resource Centres supply ready-to-use inputs; about 2,000 model demonstration farms at KVKs, agricultural universities and farmers' fields train willing farmers to prepare inputs such as jeevamrit and beejamrit; 30,000 Krishi Sakhis or community resource persons help farmers in the clusters. Farmers get a simple certification system and common branding to market natural farming produce. Guidelines were issued on 26 December 2024. In each State the mission is run by the State natural farming cell (in Andhra Pradesh, Rythu Sadhikara Samstha). The payment per farmer is not in these releases.
